To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

destabilization of the epigenome, either by genotoxic drugs or by drugs decondensing the chromatin, leads to activation of the interferon type I pathway, a response we termed TRAIN, which may contribute to the anticancer activities of these compounds.
destabilization of chromatin by small molecules, such as curaxin, can induce TRAIN, which is an interferon response to transcriptional activation of repetitive elements in the genome.
destabilization of chromatin structure by small molecule anticancer drugs induces TRAIN, which may represent a novel anticancer mechanism of these compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of epigenetic destabilization in the induction of the innate immune response and its role in the prevention and treatment of cancer.
the role of TRAIN in the epigenetic control of cellular homeostasis and the development of cancer.
the mechanisms of action and the anticancer potential of small molecules targeting the epigenome, which is a rapidly expanding field of cancer therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

destabilization of epigenetic integrity, which can be achieved with small molecules, induces TRAIN, which in turn leads to activation of interferon type I and cell death, thus providing an additional mechanism to the previously known p53-dependent mechanism of action of these drugs.
the TRAIN phenomenon is induced upon chromatin destabilization by a variety of small molecules, and that this phenomenon may be a mechanism of action of anticancer small molecule drugs.
TRAIN is a mechanism of cell elimination in response to chromosomal destabilization induced with genotoxic drugs, including curaxin and histone deacetylation inhibitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TRAIN response is a novel epigenetic surveillance mechanism which may have important implications in cancer prevention and treatment.
destabilization of chromatin structure by drugs, such as curaxin, induces the interferon response via activation of the interferon pathway genes.
TRAIN can be induced in response to chromosomal instability and/or epigenetic instability, both of which can occur as a result of exposure to genotoxic agents, including anticancer drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the epigenetic integrity is important for the cell and that its violation can be sensed and responded to.
TRAIN is a general response to chromatin desilencing.
TRAIN is induced by a variety of drugs that destabilize the chromatin structure.
